Vital Strategies “India - Tobacco Control – Main Bhi Sunita (Sunita 2.0) - Hindi”, 30 sec. Sunita, the wife of a cancer victim, speaks: "मेरे पति 18 साल की उम्र से खैनी खाया करते थे… उन्हें कैंसर नाम की खतरनाक बीमारी हो गई है". She says he is the only earner and she cannot sleep thinking about the future: "खैनी ने हमारी जिंदगी बर्बाद कर दी". The voiceover then says "खैनी, गुटका, जर्दा, पान मसाला परिवार तबाह करते हैं, तंबाकू आज ही छोड़ें" and gives the helpline, "सहायता के लिए 1800112356 पर कॉल करें". The description says it was launched in 17 languages by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Govt. of India, for airing in TV programmes and films from 10 August 2024. The main message warns about the harm of smokeless tobacco and urges quitting. It does not make any product attractive.

Ministry of Health & Family Welfare “A short anti-tobacco video on passive smoke”, 38 sec. The description says it shows how indirect or passive smoking is ruining the lives of people around you, and ends with “Quit smoking”. The English voiceover says “smoking can cost you your health and can also seriously affect the health and welfare of those around you”, then “don’t have them pay the price for your smoking”, and ends with “smoking will cost you”. The main message warns about harm to the smoker and to others, and encourages quitting. It does not make any product or brand attractive.

Vital Strategies “India - Tobacco Control - When You Quit - Hindi”, 30 sec, part of India’s anti-tobacco campaign. The Hindi voiceover says the study shows that "धूम्रपान छोड़ने के 20 मिनट बाद आपका रक्तचाप सामान्य हो जाता है", that nicotine in the body falls within days, and that within 12 months the "हृदय रोग का खतरा भी आधा रह जाता है". It then warns about the damage smoking does now and ends with "तंबाकू आज ही छोड़ें, मदद के लिए कॉल करें" and the quitline number. The main message supports quitting and warns about harm. It does not make any product or brand attractive.

Anti-tobacco campaign spot “Shadow” (India), 33 sec, posted by Vital Strategies and issued in public interest by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, with the National Tobacco Control Programme. A man smokes on a railway-station bench while a woman and two children near him cough and look unwell, with smoke stains spreading on the boy’s chest. The English voiceover says “when you smoke so did the people around you, it can irritate their eyes, bring on asthma attacks and even chest pains”, and “your smoke can cause their lung cancer”. It ends on a “Tobacco Kills – QUIT TODAY” card. The main message warns about the harm of smoking, including second-hand smoke, and urges quitting. It does not make any product or brand attractive.

Ministry of Health and Family Welfare anti-tobacco PSA “India - Sunita (Hindi) - Testimonial”, 31 sec, posted by Vital Strategies. Sunita, a 27-year-old wife and mother, speaks about oral cancer after using smokeless tobacco. The on-screen Hindi text and voiceover say "मैंने कब सोचा था मेरी जिंदगी यूं बदल जाएगी… तंबाकू ने सब कुछ बदल दिया… अब इस फैलते हुए कैंसर को मेरे चेहरे से काटना पड़ेगा". The video shows her holding a wedding photo, then a graphic surgery scene, then her face after the operation. The closing line says "खैनी, गुटखा, तंबाकू, जर्दा, पान मसाला आपका जीवन उजाड़ देते हैं", and the end card reads "तंबाकू जानलेवा है, आज ही छोड़ो". The main message warns about the harm of smokeless tobacco and urges quitting. It does not make any product attractive.

Anti-tobacco testimonial “India - Mukesh: Smokeless Tobacco Campaign (Hindi)”, 34 sec, posted by Vital Strategies and filmed at Tata Memorial Hospital, Mumbai. A doctor’s voiceover says "हम रोज 50 नए मरीज देख रहे हैं… 80 से 90 प्रतिशत मुंह के कैंसर तंबाकू चबाने से होते हैं". The video shows Mukesh Harane in a hospital bed with a feeding tube and graphic close-ups of his face, saying "मेरा नाम मुकेश है… अब मुझे कैंसर हुआ है… शायद मैं बोल नहीं सकूंगा". A caption notes his death. The narrator says "अफसोस, मुकेश बच नहीं सका और वो सिर्फ 24 साल का था", then lists "खैनी, पान, गुटका", and the video ends on a black card reading "तम्बाकू जानलेवा है". The main message warns about the harm of smokeless tobacco and discourages use. It does not make any product attractive.

The main message links the pan masala brand with success, sport and inspiration, so it makes the brand attractive. A tiny line of on-screen text does not change that, so I labelled it promotional.

“Vimal Elaichi - Ajay Devgn | Shahrukh Khan | Akshay Kumar I Hindi TVC 45 secs”, 45 sec, uploaded by the brand’s channel (Vimal Elaichi). A stylish star-led film with three men in a white convertible, a call up to a woman on a balcony, and red saffron-like particles falling through the scenes. The Hindi subtitles include "ओए नीचे आ, घोड़े बेच दिए क्या" and "केसरिया के दीवाने", and it ends with a Vimal Elaichi pack shot and the slogan "बोलो जुबाँ केसरी". The title names the three film stars. The main message makes the brand attractive through celebrity glamour and a catchy slogan, so I labelled it promotional. I saw no health warning, only small text saying the saffron shown is a creative depiction.

“Raj Niwas Pan Masala TVC 30 secs”, about 30 sec, uploaded by the brand’s own channel (Raj Niwas Pan Masala). A glamorous royal-style film: a palace and gardens, a man in a dark suit and a woman in an embellished dress on a veranda, two riders on horseback, and a car scene where a hand holds the sachet with the line “Maharaja ki pasand”. A man in sunglasses and leather gloves tips the sachet into his mouth, so consumption is shown. It ends on the “Raj Niwas Flavoured Pan Masala” pack shot with a small line of text saying chewing pan masala is harmful to health, not for minors, and 0% tobacco. The main message makes the pan masala brand attractive and shows it being used, so I labelled it promotional

“Dilbagh Pan Masala - TVC by Basic Communications”, 15 sec, a TV commercial for Dilbagh Royal Pan Masala posted by the ad agency. A man in a dark suit enjoys a meal at a restaurant, then tips a pan masala sachet into his mouth, so consumption is shown. It ends on a pack shot of "दिलबाग रॉयल पान मसाला" against a golden glitter background. A small on-screen warning reads “Chewing of pan masala is injurious to health, not for minors” throughout. The main message makes the brand attractive and shows the product being used, so I labelled it promotional. The small required warning does not change that.

“Shikhar Pan Masala TVC”, about 60 sec, uploaded by the brand’s own channel. A cinematic film of a man in a suit with a car on a coastal road, a desert, an engineer in a hard hat at sunset, a wind turbine and a village lit up at night. It ends on a pack shot of “Shikhar Pan Masala” with the tagline "जो दिल की सुनते हैं, वो शिखर पर रहते हैं". The main message links the pan masala brand to ambition, success and progress, so it makes the brand attractive. A small on-screen line says chewing pan masala is injurious to health, contains 0% tobacco and is not for minors. This required warning does not change the main message, so I labelled it promotional.

“Ganesh Pan Masala TVC”, about 36 sec, a Tamil-language TV commercial for Ganesh 701 scented supari / pan masala, uploaded by a film production channel (Yaanus Films). The title card reads “GANESH 701 Scented Supari – 30 sec Tamil 11.09.09”. A man in a black leather jacket and sunglasses holds up a yellow Ganesh 701 sachet while a festive crowd cheers around him. The closing Tamil line on screen reads "பெயரே கேட்டாலே சும்மா அதிருதில்ல" (just hearing the name sends a thrill), shown with the Ganesh 701 logo. The main message makes the brand exciting and attractive through a celebrity-style hero and crowd energy. I saw no health warning in the frames I checked, so I labelled it promotional.

“Dilbagh Pan Masala Diwali TVC”, 10 sec, a Diwali greeting commercial uploaded by the ad agency (Basic Communications). A "दिलबाग रॉयल पान मसाला" pack is shown throughout, with fireworks and diyas appearing around it. The Hindi voiceover and subtitles say "दिलबाग की तरफ से आप सभी को दीपावली की हार्दिक शुभकामनाएं" and end with the slogan "दिलबाग पान मसाला, दिल है तो जोश है". A small on-screen line says chewing pan masala is injurious to health and not for minors. The main message ties the brand name and slogan to a festive greeting, which makes the brand attractive

“Goa Pan Masala | #kamyabikikick | TVC (45 sec) | Sanjay Dutt, Ravi Kishan & Krushna Abhishek”, 45 sec, uploaded by the brand’s own channel (Goa Pan Masala). A comedy-style celebrity ad: a man in a blue blazer and sunglasses talks to the camera and puts a Goa sachet to his mouth, other men talk next to a sports car, and a shopkeeper holds up a sachet. It ends on a pack shot with the line “Oonchi Khushboo.. Ooncha Swad..!” and price bursts of ₹10 and ₹5. The description names the three film stars and the campaign “Kamyabi Ki Kick”. The main message makes the brand attractive through star power, humour and a low price, and shows the product being used. I saw no health warning in the frames I checked, so I labelled it promotional.

This is a 60-second TVC (MATES upload) for Pan Vilas Pan Masala, starring Manoj Bajpayee. It opens on a heritage mansion with the on-screen text “PAN VILAS – NAWAB”. It then shows the lead in a cream kurta in a period “Nawabi” setting: a man reading a newspaper headed “Second Innings”, rooftop scenes with attendants holding an umbrella, and a hall full of people. The Hindi subtitles are fragmentary. They include "गांव में", "दूध वाले को चाय तक पापा कम हो तो" and "है और", plus [संगीत] music cues. The ad builds an aspirational, royal, premium image around the Pan Vilas brand and a celebrity face, which makes the product attractive. There is no warning or discouragement in any frame I sampled (2s, 12s, 22s, 32s, 42s, 52s, 62s, 66s), and the last frame at 69s is black. I did not check the exact end-card frame, so a small legal or health line there is possible. It would not change the label, because the main message sells the product and normalizes its use.

This is a 30-second Indian public-health PSA from Vital Strategies. The description says it ran in 2020 to support the ban on spitting and on smokeless tobacco in public places, and it urges people to quit tobacco to fight COVID-19. It opens in a village tea stall, where a man in a pink shirt sits among others. Then comes a rural courtyard scene with a woman cooking and a man in a yellow shirt. In a doctor’s clinic, a patient in a cream shirt, with a doctor facing him, repeats the English-subtitled line “I don’t believe that tobacco kills.” That line is then undercut by a graphic, red-toned close-up of an operation, with the subtitle “that tobacco kills. Some people…”. After that, the same man lies in a hospital bed in a white sheet, with his wife, an older woman and a young girl in a yellow top standing beside him. The ad ends on a black end card reading “QUIT TOBACCO – FIGHT CORONAVIRUS”, with the toll-free quitline “1-800-11-2356”, a missed-call number “011-22901701”, and the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and National Tobacco Control Programme logos. The closing subtitle says “Quit tobacco and stay healthy to fight coronavirus.” The whole message warns about harm, discourages use and supports quitting, and nothing in it makes tobacco attractive.

This is a 36-second anti-smoking TVC from Vital Strategies about secondhand smoke. Its title card reads “VITAL STRATEGIES – ANTI SMOKING TVC (SICKENING) – 30 SEC – ENGLISH – 01.03.17”. The first scene is a doctor’s consultation. A woman in a red saree sits at a desk, and the English auto-subtitle reads “he’s having trouble…”. Next, a shirtless teenage boy is examined as the subtitles say “he’s having trouble breathing, let’s take a look during an asthma…”. The next frames show him wincing and holding his chest as the subtitles explain that the muscles around the airways tighten and swell. Then come “uncontrollable coughing and difficulty breathing”. The ad ends on a black end card with the text “TOBACCO KILLS – QUIT TODAY!” and a no-smoking sign over a smouldering ashtray, with the logos of the health ministry and Vital Strategies. The last subtitle, “smoking around others is sickening, quit today”, gives the main message that smoking harms other people and that smokers should quit. The ad shows no attractive use of tobacco, so it is purely a warning that discourages use.

This is a 30-second Hindi anti-smoking PSA. The video description says the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, with technical support from World Lung Foundation, launched the “Artery” campaign in January 2014 to warn about smoking damage to the heart. It opens on a close-up of a man’s hand, with a gold ring, holding a cigarette. Next, a man in a light shirt stands on a street beside a sign reading “PLEASE THROW USED CIGARETTE BUTTS IN WHITE BUCKET”. The ad then cuts to a surgical-style scene in which gloved hands on a green cloth hold a reddish artery. The next close-ups show the artery clogged with yellow fatty plaque, and then the plaque lifted out beside the artery. A dark smoke shot follows. The ad ends on a black end card with the Hindi text "तम्बाकू जानलेवा है – आज ही छोड़ो" (“Tobacco is deadly – quit today”), a no-smoking sign, and the logos of the health ministry and the National Tobacco Control Programme. The message links smoking to damaged arteries and death and urges viewers to quit. The cigarette in the opening only sets up the harm, and nothing in the ad makes smoking attractive

This is a 36-second Hindi anti-tobacco PSA (“I Don’t Believe”, 05.10.16) issued by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and the National Tobacco Control Programme. Village men sit talking, and one of them repeats «मैं नहीं मानता कि तंबाकू जानलेवा है». A graphic surgical close-up follows, and then the same man lies in a hospital bed with a worried girl and an older woman beside him. A voice says «चाहे हम कुछ भी कहें, कुछ लोग हमारा संदेश नहीं सुनते», and the ad closes with «तंबाकू जानलेवा है। यह चेतावनी हर पैक पर है। इसे पढ़िए और इस पर विश्वास कीजिए». The end card shows a smokeless tobacco pouch inside a prohibition sign, with the text «तम्बाकू जानलेवा है – इसे पढ़िए». It warns about the harm and discourages use, and nothing in it makes tobacco attractive.

This is a 38-second Hindi anti-tobacco PSA from Vital Strategies. It opens on a title card reading “WHAT DAMAGE WILL THIS CIGARETTE DO – HINDI – 30 SEC – 290518”. Weathered hands open a pack of cigarettes, and the shots that follow show a man being spoon-fed by a woman beside the Hindi word «स्ट्रोक», and a man lying ill in a hospital bed. The ad then returns to the hands with the Hindi question in red and white, «यह सिगरेट या बीड़ी पीने का क्या परिणाम होगा?». The end card reads «तम्बाकू आज ही छोड़ें» next to a no-smoking sign, followed by «सहायता के लिए कॉल करें 1-800-11-2356 (टोल फ्री) या मिस्ड कॉल दें 011-22901701». The health ministry and National Tobacco Control Programme logos appear at the bottom. The ad links cigarette and bidi use to stroke and serious illness and urges viewers to quit with a helpline, so it warns about harm and discourages use. The cigarettes appear only to set up the harm, not to make smoking appealing.

This is a 34-second English anti-tobacco PSA from Vital Strategies about the benefits of quitting. It begins on a black frame, and then a man in a yellow shirt sits in an armchair with an ashtray on the table beside him. The English subtitles read “quit smoking, your body…”. Next, a family eats dinner together at a table (a man in a green kurta, a woman, a boy and a girl) with the subtitle “your blood pressure goes down in a few days, your sense…”. The ad then shows the man in a green T-shirt jogging in a park, with “attack and lung cancer is…”. An anatomical heart appears next, with “you’re a heart attack waiting”. After that, a woman in a red dupatta stands crying in a hospital-style corridor, with a [Music] cue and “every beedi cigarette is doing you damage”. The ad ends on “quit today”. The message tells smokers that quitting brings health benefits and that every cigarette or beedi causes damage, so it supports quitting and discourages use. The cigarette and ashtray in the first scene only set up the harm, and nothing makes smoking attractive.

This is a 3-minute (3:02) film by FCB Ulka for the Mumbai Traffic Police, with the description “Be a responsible friend”. It opens on a crowded tenement courtyard with neighbours watching from the balconies. Later shots show a woman crying among mourners, and a man in a white shirt sitting on a plastic chair among a crowd with flowers beside him, as at a funeral. A flashback shows friends toasting with whisky glasses in a bar. A man in a white shirt walks alone down a lane, and another man in a cream shirt is on a phone call looking uneasy. The film ends on the on-screen tagline “BE A RESPONSIBLE FRIEND. CALL A CAB AFTER THE PARTY.” The main message warns about the harm of drinking and driving and tells viewers to take a cab after drinking. The drinks appear only as the cause of the loss, and nothing makes alcohol attractive.

This is a roughly 2-minute (1:59) road-safety film, “Yamaraj – Drink and Get Driven”, uploaded by Saurabh M. More. According to the description, the Zara Tapas Bar in Chennai made it with the Chennai Traffic Police and McCann-Erickson, and it is about drunk driving. It opens on an illuminated temple gopuram at night. Then it shows the “Zara – The Tapas Bar” entrance with the on-screen text “THIS TIME,”, followed by “SPIRITED PATRONS USING THE VALET SERVICE WERE IN FOR A SURPRISE” over a man on a phone call. A blurred, fast shot of a car window follows, and then patrons are seen waiting outside at night. In a later scene a woman gets her car from a valet, with a white vehicle in front and a “no parking” sign behind. The last sampled frame shows laughing patrons. The description says that Yama, the Hindu god of death, quietly arrives in the patrons’ cars when the valet brings them back, to scare drinkers into using a driver-for-hire service instead. The message warns about drunk-driving deaths and pushes viewers to use a driver, so it discourages drink-driving. Alcohol is only the setting for the stunt, and nothing makes it attractive.

This is a roughly 4.5-minute (4:34) corporate sustainability film from Diageo India’s own channel. The description says it covers the company’s “Society 2030” plan to curb underage drinking, raise awareness against drink-driving and promote moderation, including work with 25 Regional Transport Offices. It opens on a “PROMOTE POSITIVE DRINKING” badge over an amber liquid background. A man in a Diageo polo shirt speaks to the camera in front of the on-screen text “CURBING UNDERAGE CONSUMPTION”. Later shots show an online survey page headed “A FEW QUICK QUESTIONS…” about young people’s attitudes to alcohol, and an aerial view of students sitting in a circle on a green mat at a workshop. People queue outside a mobile unit with “Behaviour…” branding for what appears to be a drink-driving awareness activity, and the final scenes show night traffic with a car and motorbikes, with a subtitle ending “after consuming alcohol”. The film ends on a white “DIAGEO – Celebrating life, every day, everywhere” card. The message is about responsible drinking, with an anti-underage-drinking and anti-drink-driving focus, so it warns about harm. No alcohol product or brand is shown being consumed or made attractive. The only brand element is the company name and slogan at the end.

This is a 54-second TV commercial for McDowell’s No.1 Platinum Soda, uploaded by the brand’s own channel (McDNo1Platinum). The title names MS Dhoni, and the description says it celebrates the Indian cricket team’s success at the Champions Trophy 2013. It opens on a black title card with a mirrored face on both sides of the McDowell’s No.1 Platinum logo and the text “45 SECONDS – 22 10 2013”. The film then cuts between a close-up of a man in a stadium-style setting with the on-screen text “23rd June”, a man in a suit in a dark space, and a mirrored shot of hands clasped, with subtitles such as “a turning point in” and “told me to go with the informed spinner, but I had”. Cricket scenes follow: a batter bending in a floodlit stadium, a wide view of a pitch, and a batter in a helmet raising a gloved fist, with the subtitle “but to be successful you”. It ends on a black screen with the subtitle “different not dowels number one platinum soda, the number one spirit of leadership” (the auto-caption mis-hears “McDowell’s”). The ad links the brand to cricket success and leadership through a celebrity, which makes the brand attractive. I saw no health warning in the frames I checked, and the end shows no pack.

“Ranveer Singh Motivational Video | Royal Stag Music CD’s TVC”, 102 sec, a compilation of Royal Stag ads uploaded by a third-party channel (ASF Productions). A “Ranveer Singh Royal Stag Advertisement” title card opens it, and the Royal Stag logo stays on screen in nearly every frame. The scenes show a man in a white shirt in an office, a man in a crowd of people filming with phones, a luxury car at night, a bearded man on a stage with blue lights and a live band performing. The on-screen slogan reads “IT’S YOUR LIFE. MAKE IT LARGE.” and the end shows the “ROYAL STAG – MEGA MUSIC” logo with a “Music CDs” tag. The Hindi subtitles are garbled, so I did not quote them. The main message links the whisky brand to celebrity glamour, music and success, so it makes the brand attractive.

Ministry of Health and Family Welfare anti-tobacco spot “Child” (PIB India), 38 sec, released under the COTPA rules to be screened in films with smoking scenes. The title card reads “Child – SmokeFree – Eng – 30 sec”. A little girl draws a family picture with the word “Love” on it, then looks up worried at her father at a restaurant table, and later a man is seen behind a frosted door with a faint “smoking” caption. The father is last shown on a sofa with the girl and an older woman. The main message is a warning about the harm of smoking to the family, especially children, and it discourages use. No brand appears, and nothing makes tobacco attractive.

10-second Ministry of Health & Family Welfare video, “To quit tobacco, call the Quitline number 1800-112-356 today!” (#SayNoToTobacco). The description says “Choose health over the dangerous habit of tobacco. Your life is worth more than a risky addiction.” The screen shows a still graphic with the Government of India emblem and “Ministry of Health and Family Welfare”, the headline “CHOOSE LIFE NOT SMOKE”, a cigarette whose filter-end is drawn as a row of black human figures like a crowd, and the line “To quit tobacco, call the Quitline number 1800-112-356”. The message discourages smoking and tells viewers to call the quitline, and nothing makes tobacco attractive.

Ministry of Health and Family Welfare anti-smoking spot “Dhuan” (PIB India), 37 sec, released under the COTPA rules for screening in films with smoking scenes. A title card reads “Dhuan – SmokeFree – Hindi – 30 sec”. A smoky restaurant scene shows diners at tables with smoke drifting and an older man resting his head on his hand, while other diners eat with smoke around them. A close-up shows a young man with an upset look at a plate of samosas and a drink while a hand holding a cigarette sits beside him. A sign reads “No Smoking Area – Smoking here is an offence”, with a prohibition symbol. The end card shows a no-smoking symbol with the Hindi slogan «धूम्रमुक्त» (“smoke-free”), the National Tobacco Control Programme and Ministry logos, and «द्वारा जनहित में जारी» (“issued in public interest by”). The main message is that smoking in public places harms others and is an offence, so it discourages use. No brand appears, and nothing makes tobacco attractive.

“India – Tobacco Control – Benefits of Quitting and Tobacco Cessation – English” (Vital Strategies), 2 min 24 sec. According to the description, it promotes the health benefits of quitting tobacco and the cessation services of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and it was launched on 9 October 2025 under the 60-day Tobacco Free Youth Campaign 3.0, with technical support from Vital Strategies and WHO India. It opens with an auto-rickshaw driver in white clothes sitting in his vehicle. An anatomy graphic then shows a man’s body labelled with tobacco-related diseases: mouth, throat, lung, stomach, pancreatic and kidney cancer, stroke, blindness/cataract, heart disease, asthma, COPD and impotence. Later scenes show an office worker at a desk with a family photo, a smiling man on a park bench, and a couple on a sofa with the subtitle “reduces by half. By quitting, you not only protect your health and shield…”. A woman counsellor wearing a headset sits in front of a “QUIT TOBACCO” poster with the subtitle “counseling from trained counselors in multiple…”, and the final scene shows a man in a blue shirt saying “a daily plan and continued support.” The message lists the harms of tobacco, explains the benefits of quitting and offers quitting support. It is preventive, and nothing in it makes tobacco attractive.

“Tulsi Pan Masala | Tulsi pan masala old doordarshan ads”, 65 sec, a vintage 90s Doordarshan commercial for Tulsi pan masala, uploaded by “90s time travels” (the description names the actors Rohit Roy and Aditi Govitrikar). A smiling young man in a blue jacket leans out of a car window in a busy city street. The scenes follow with a man in an orange vest and yellow tie dancing between cars, a street clogged with cars and a wedding-style procession with a decorated umbrella, and a rooftop dance with a crowd in colourful clothes, with music cues in the captions. In the closing scene, a silver “Tulsi Mix” sachet appears, with the Hindi tagline «असली मज़े की मस्त लहर» and a second tagline line that reads like “Ab ayega asli mazaa!”. The ad ties the pan masala brand to fun, celebration and music, so it makes the brand attractive and encourages use.

“TVC || Television Ads || Kamla Pasand Pan masala”, 38 sec, uploaded by the ad agency Audvik Solutions. A party scene shows a man in a brown sherwani holding a green Kamla Pasand tin, with women in sarees around him and a woman offering a tray of pan masala, and the Hindi subtitles run as a jingle: «कुछ सुनाइए ना पहले तो मूड बनाने का साधन हो», «बरसों की साधना ने दिया कमला पसंद», «पान मसाले को बेमिसाल स्वाद और अनूप जी को मधुर आवाज़ ऐसी लागी», «इसके स्वाद और खुशबू से दिल मचलने लगा कमला पसंद पान मसाला», and the closing «मूड बन जाता है कमला पसंद पान मसाला स्वाद में हमेशा दो कदम आगे». The end card shows the “Kamla Pasand Pan Masala” tin and sachet with the Hindi brand name «कमला पसंद» and a faint statutory-warning line at the bottom. The ad links the brand to taste, fragrance, a party mood and being “two steps ahead”, and the man is shown holding the tin and tasting the product. That makes the brand attractive and encourages use, so it is promotional

“Rajshree Pan Masala Ad - Annu Kapoor” (the actor’s name is from the title), 138 sec, a compilation of Rajshree Pan Masala TV spots uploaded by “The Rtist”. Each spot has a man in a different setting speaking to the camera with a social message tied to the brand. A road scene runs on the subtitle «…शराब पीने के बाद गाड़ी…», a hospital ward scene shows a patient lying on a bed, and the next spot opens with «रक्तदान कीजिए राजश्री पैन मसाला जो मां-बाप…». Then come a park scene with a man and girls playing with a ball («यह बेटियां…») and a cupboard scene with the line «राजश्री पैन मसाला अपने पुराने कपड़ों को यूँ ही पुराना समझकर फेंकना…». The subtitle «…होगा राजश्री पैन मसाला» closes one spot. The ads use health and social themes to build goodwill around the Rajshree Pan Masala name. They never discourage pan masala use, and the brand is the closing line of every spot, so the main message makes the brand attractive

“Blenders Pride”, 54 sec, a TVC uploaded by an individual channel (Ruchika Khanna) with the description “Blenders Pride TVC. Speaks for itself.” The opening card shows the Seagram’s “Blenders Pride – Magical Nights” logo with the date “27022008”. A short romantic story follows, mostly with music and laughter in the captions. A woman sits on a night bus, a red tram passes on a night street, and a man plays a violin to a woman in a gown on a stone staircase. A young man types on a laptop in a bedroom, a “Happy Birthday” gift tag appears, and a man and woman share a quiet moment before a bridge lit up at night. The tagline reads “Speaks for itself” with the “Music CDs” tag, and the closing subtitle is «Seagram’s Blenders Pride music speaks for itself». The ad ties the whisky brand to romance, music and a glamorous night out. It never discourages drinking, so the main message makes the brand attractive

“Officer’s Choice Blue TVC”, 47 sec, uploaded by Keroscene Films. Officer’s Choice Blue is a whisky brand of Allied Blenders and Distillers (ABD), so this is indirect, brand-image advertising for an alcohol brand. It shows no bottle, glass or drinking and no substitute product, so it is not a classic surrogate ad (like soda or music CDs). Instead it sells the brand name through an emotional “unsung heroes” story. Two uniformed policemen direct traffic beside a police car, and office scenes lead to a birthday celebration with a cake and clapping colleagues. The English captions run: «They stand tall, for… right and wrong is remembered… heroes before… crown of joy looks best on others’ heart. Officer’s Choice». The ad ends on the ABD logo. It links the whisky brand to honour, selflessness and celebration, which makes the brand attractive, and there is no warning or discouraging message.

“Pan Parag Pan Masala”, 30 sec TVC on the brand’s own channel (PanParag), with the description “Dhoom Macha De.. Rang Jama De!!”. It follows an “India rising” story. A young man types on a laptop in a car, with the Hindi subtitles «एक नया इंडिया जागा कामयाब», then a man works on a laptop at night on an outdoor table, a rocket-launch control room appears, a businesswoman sits in front of a world map, and a cricket match with a batter in a blue shirt is shown. One scene shows the man in the car tipping a small sachet into his mouth, so consumption is shown. The subtitles run «जागा कामयाब इंडिया, जागा आगे बढ़ता इंडिया, राइज़िंग अपना इंडिया पहचान बना का इंडिया ग्लोबल अपना इंडिया मचा दे न जमाने इंडिया». The end card shows the Pan Parag range (Supreme tin, Premium and Sachet packs) with the slogans “Dhoom Macha De.. Rang Jama De!” and “The Choice of Young India”, a “0% tobacco” mark and the small statutory line “CHEWING OF PAN MASALA IS INJURIOUS TO HEALTH. NOT FOR MINOR NON NUTRITIVE PRODUCT”. The ad ties the pan masala brand to national pride, success and youth, and shows the product being used, which makes it attractive and normalizes use. The small required warning does not change that.

“Pan Bahar – Pierce Brosnan TVC”, 60 sec, on the brand’s own channel (Pan Bahar – Pehchan Kamyabi Ki). The description says “Class Never Goes Out Of Style!” and that the brand roped in Pierce Brosnan (the name comes from the title and description). A glamorous black-tie story opens on a grand hotel at night. A man in a tuxedo steps out of an orange sports car, and a guest in a tuxedo takes a small blue tin from his pocket. A woman in a red dress looks back at him in a hall with red curtains. A man in a tuxedo walks across a marble hall under chandeliers, and in the closing scenes he holds up the tin, smiling to the camera. The captions include «agent», «so» and «class never goes out of…». The end card shows the “PAN BAHAR – PEHCHAN KAMYABI KI” logo, a Pan Bahar tin marked “NO TOBACCO NICOTINE”, the brand’s social-media handles, and the closing line “class never goes out of style”. The ad ties the pan masala brand to luxury, elegance and celebrity glamour, which makes it attractive. I saw no health warning

“8PM Whisky TVC India”, 98 sec, an archive upload by “Scrapbook Of Dejavu”. An opening title card reads “8PM Whisky TVC India – Brand: Radico Khaitan – Year: 1999 – Duration: 90 Sec – Director: Ravi K. Chandran”. The ad is a black-and-white wartime story, with officers in peaked caps and uniforms against barbed wire and watchtowers. The scenes show a grave officer in profile, a heavy-set officer speaking sternly and a woman soldier carrying a tray of glasses to an officer who is opening a bottle. An officer then holds up a glass of whisky with ice, looking at the camera, and two officers sit beside a bottle and a glass on a crate. The film ends on a black screen. This is a direct alcohol ad, not a surrogate. It shows the whisky being poured and held in a glass and ties the brand to camaraderie and a stylish, dramatic story, which normalizes drinking and makes the brand attractiv

“Haywards 5000 Club Soda – TVC – Rohiet Nair”, 54 sec, an actor’s portfolio upload (the description says it was his first TV commercial, with Diganth, J Karthik and Rohiet Nair). A title card reads “Haywards 5000 Soda – The Interview – 45 sec – Hindi – 270306”, over bottles in ice. The story is a comic job interview in a car, where three young men grill another man, with Hindi subtitles such as «मेरे भाई चल बाहर होके आते हैं कुछ करते हो हां बैंक में मैं मैनेजर» (“my brother, let’s go out, do you do something? yes, I’m a manager at a bank”) and «फ्री टाइम में रीडिंग इंटरनेट». The punchline is a “Soda” pack shot of an ice-cold red Haywards 5000 bottle with the subtitle «ठंडा वन डालोगे एक हेव 5000 सोडा अरे यह तो सॉलिड निकला» (“you’ll pour a cold one, a Haywards 5000 soda, hey, this is solid”). A “TOO MUCH SOLID” graphic and «दूध 5000 सोडा सचमुच सॉलिड» («Haywards 5000 Soda, really solid») close it, and the end shows the bottle labelled “HAYWARDS 5000 SUPER STRONG SODA”. The ad promotes the soda under the “5000” brand name and ties it to a cool, “solid” young-male image, which makes the brand attractive. It is a surrogate-style ad for the beer, with no health warning

“Raag Pan Masala TVC hindi 2016”, 41 sec, a production-house upload by KSILENT PRODUCTIONS. The description credits Godfrey Phillips India Ltd. as the client and “Raag” as the brand. The ad is a stylised paper-cutout animation in the style of Mughal miniature paintings. A sunset sky and a patterned sea open it, and a royal barge with a canopy carries a king, a courtier and a woman. A man sits cross-legged between two camels with a signboard in Devanagari script. A man in a blue turban holds a “RAAG” pan masala pack in his hand, and the barge sails past a red fort. The ad ends on a pink-green cloud scene with a “PAN VILAS – RAAG Premium Pan Masala” pack and the on-screen slogan “Swad Mein Heera” (“a diamond in taste”). The ad ties the pan masala brand to royalty, luxury and taste, which makes it attractive

“Wills Cigarettes TV commercial from 1980’s India”, 66 sec, uploaded by WildFilmsIndia, a stock-footage archive (a “www.wildfilmsindia.com” watermark covers the video). The description says the commercial is now banned in India but ran in the 1980s for Wills filter cigarettes, and it jokes “Made for each other, anyone?”. The story is a series of lifestyle scenes: a close-up of a smiling man, a man in a pink shirt with a sweater over his shoulders leaning on a library desk, a bridegroom in a pink turban with flower garlands, a man in a white T-shirt at a book-stacked table, and a man cooking in a yellow shirt and apron in a bright kitchen. A woman in a yellow outfit hangs a red balloon and streamers at a party. A couple relaxes on a balcony sofa, the man lighting a cigarette while the woman reads a book. The English captions run «intelligent you looked», «didn’t you look so», «funny», «proud» and, in the final scene, «filter and tobacco perfectly matched and now». The final frame is a black stock-footage licence card. The ad ties the cigarette brand to happy, caring couples and a stylish home life and shows a man lighting up, which makes smoking look attractive and normal, so it is promotional

“100 Pipers Commercial for India. 1994.”, 65 sec, uploaded by “robbieswales”. The description says it is a 100 Pipers Scotch whisky commercial filmed and shown in India in 1994. It opens on black, then shows a lake and green hills at dusk, a man fishing in a stream, and a fisherman by a lake under a pink-orange sky. The next scenes show two glasses of whisky with golden lights behind them, then a man in a tweed jacket drinking from a glass and looking at the camera. The English captions run as a story: «years of fishing my father used to say you hands you catch it with your mind», «with the taste buds in your ears according to a Scottish…», «taste a scotch whisky you can hear a piper play only when it’s exceptional» and «Scotch whisky every sip is pure music flat or sharp can I hear them». A pack shot shows a Seagram’s “100 PIPERS DE LUXE SCOTCH WHISKY” bottle beside two glasses of whisky with the on-screen slogan “Seagram – Every sip is pure music”. The ad ties the whisky to taste, heritage and “pure music” and shows a man drinking it, which makes alcohol attractive and normalizes use. I saw no health warning. It is a direct whisky ad, not a surrogate ad.

“Anti-Smoking Ad in India”, 50 sec, uploaded by “justnewhere” (description: “Award winning Anti-Smoking Ad from India”). It is a short bus story in vintage film quality. Elderly men in white turbans sit in a crowded bus, and a young man in a khaki shirt stands holding the rail. Other passengers stand to give up their seats and help the young man as he sits down. The English captions explain the twist: «7even minutes of his life every time he smokes a cigarette be nice to smokers they don’t have much time left». Passengers treat the smoker kindly because each cigarette shortens his life. The ad closes on a black card with the “Cancer Patients Aid Association” logo. The main message warns that smoking shortens life, and it discourages use. It shows no brand, and nothing makes smoking attractive.

“A short Anti-Tobacco film – Students Manubhai Patel Dental College”, 4 min 42 sec, uploaded by Manubhai Patel Dental College, Vadodara. The description says it is a student film against tobacco use that won 2nd prize in a World Cancer Day video competition. A title card reads “MANUBHAI PATEL DENTAL COLLEGE PRESENTS – SHORT FILM ON ANTI TOBACCO”. The first scenes show two students on a campus bench. One is on a phone call, and the other talks to him urgently. Later a woman in a white doctor’s coat speaks to the camera against a plain wall, and another scene shows a close-up of an open mouth with a finger pressing on the tongue, which is an oral-cancer check. The closing credits read “GUIDED BY – DR. RASHMI GS PHULARI, DR. ARPAN SHAH, DR. DHARMESH SHAH, DR. DIPEN PATEL” and “AND DEPARTMENT OF ORAL PATHOLOGY AND MICROBIOLOGY”. The film warns about the harm of tobacco, with an oral-health message, and it discourages use. It shows no brand, and nothing makes tobacco attractive

“India – Mukesh Smokeless Tobacco Campaign (English) – Testimonial” (Vital Strategies), 34 sec. The description says it features 24-year-old Mukesh Harane from Maharashtra, who dies from his chewing addiction, and was filmed at Tata Memorial Hospital in Mumbai. A title card reads “SMOKELESS TOBACCO (MUKESH) TVC – 30 sec – ENGLISH – 18 12 2010”. A doctor’s voice says: «we are seeing about 50 patients a day» and «80 to 90% of our oral cancer patients are from chewing tobacco». Mukesh then appears in a hospital bed with a feeding tube, captioned “Mukesh Harane – Oral cancer patient”, and says: «I am Mukesh. I chewed Gutka for only one year… and now I am getting operated for oral cancer». A caption reads “Mukesh Harane – Died 27th October 2009”, and the narration says he «could not be saved and he was only 24». The closing subtitle names «pan gutka pan masala killers» over a black “Tobacco Kills” card. The main message warns that chewing tobacco causes oral cancer and death, and it discourages use. It shows no brand, and nothing makes tobacco attractive.

“Union Health Secretary’s Message on World No Tobacco Day”, 3 min 16 sec, from the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare channel. The description says the Union Health Secretary addresses tobacco use in India on World No Tobacco Day 2024, citing 13 lakh preventable deaths a year and heavy economic costs. It lists India’s actions and focus areas for 2024: strict enforcement of COTPA 2003, intensified awareness campaigns and tobacco-free environments. The video is one continuous shot of a man in a light-blue shirt seated at a desk with his hands clasped, in front of a wall of name plaques, with the ministry logo at the top left and the “WORLD NO TOBACCO DAY” banner at the bottom. The English captions include «tobacco control law, COTPA 2003 intensified». The message promotes tobacco control and discourages tobacco use. It shows no brand, and nothing makes tobacco attractive.

A0026 (152s) YouTube upload "Akshay Kumar OLD Ad - Red & White" by The Marketing Intern, an archived re-upload of an old Indian cigarette commercial. Product: cigarette | Brand: Red & White. Burned-in overlay text on every sampled frame: "Akshay Kumar - Red & White Ad". Scenes: misty mountain landscape, a car on a hill road, a man in sunglasses leaning out of a red vehicle with a cigarette in his mouth, a lively dance party with a group of men and women at a poolside or terrace, women dancing in a red cabin, a man in a red check shirt doing a stunt hanging from a wire, a romantic candlelit dinner with a cocktail. The ad ties smoking to adventure, glamour, youth and celebrity charm, which makes the brand attractive and normalizes use. No health warning or anti-tobacco message was seen in the sampled frames. Marked as a surrogate-free direct tobacco ad, but note it is an archived third-party upload with a creator-added overlay, so it could be excluded under strict rules for non-original ads

"Retro Indian ad for Chancellor Cigarettes, featuring Tiger Pataudi!" by Friday Night At The Movies, an archived vintage Indian cigarette commercial. Product: cigarette | Brand: Chancellor Cigarettes. Scenes: a man in white shirt and trousers walking on a green lawn near white pillars, a lavishly laid breakfast table with fruit, juice and silver serving ware, an old-style study with a lamp, framed pictures, a matchbox and a lit cigarette on a desk, a man in a dark jacket speaking while holding his hands together, and two men in an evening-wear setting with a cigarette in the mouth. On-screen end slogan on a gold tray with a matchbox, cigarette holder and candle: "A cigarette so distinguished, it's by appointment to your..." (the line is cut off at the bottom of the frame, so the last word is not read). The ad frames smoking as an aristocratic, refined, premium lifestyle and makes the brand desirable. No health warning or anti-tobacco message was seen in the sampled frames. The uploader's channel logo is overlaid and an outro card follows from about 83s. Third-party archive upload of an original ad, so it could be excluded under strict rules for non-original uploads.

"Short Film on Tobacco (Hindi)" by Quit Nasha, a tobacco-free advocacy film by World Lung Foundation (title card: "Tobacco Free advocacy film / World Lung Foundation / Language: Hindi / Total Run Time: 04 Minutes 35 Seconds"). Product: tobacco, cigarette and smokeless | Brand: not_applicable. The film uses burned-in Hindi subtitles over first-person testimonies and clinical scenes: a man speaking to camera (30s), a young woman with the subtitle "कभी तंबाकू चबाने से होने वाला कैंसर बहुत छोटे उम्र में भी हो सकते" (110s), an on-screen stat "35% ADULTS OF AGE 26+" with the subtitle "भारत में लगभग 27 करोड़ 50 लाख लोग तंबाकू का सेवन करते हैं" (150s), a hospital patient captioned "Vinay Kumar Dixit (28 years) Patient (Oral Cancer)" with the subtitle "2000 को पता चला है कि इनको कैंसर है बायोप्सी रिपोर्ट के" (190s), and a man with a throat stoma hole saying "मैं 1966 में सिगरेट पीना शुरू किया मेरा जो सांस नहीं" (230s). End card: warning-style sign with "TOBACCO KILLS / Make India Tobacco Free" (262s), subtitle "रखें देश को तंबाकू मुक्त", then World Lung Foundation credits (279s). Preventive: it shows oral cancer, a throat stoma and early-age disease in real patients, gives prevalence statistics, and ends with a call to make India tobacco free, with no product promotion at all.

Tamil short film “Aaraam Viral (ஆறாம் விரல்) - Smoking Awareness Short Film”, 580 seconds, uploaded by Govt. Sivagangai Medical College & Hospital. The film opens with a health advisory card: “SMOKING CAUSE CANCER - SMOKING KILLS!” with the Tamil line "புகை பிடிப்பது புற்று நோயை உண்டாக்கும் மற்றும் உயிரை கொல்லும்", plus “LIQUOR DRINKING IS INJURIOUS TO HEALTH”. The visuals show an animated DNA and cell-damage sequence, young men in a hostel room, a lab bottle with microscopic organisms, and hospital scenes with a patient on a bed and a doctor. It ends with a “Be Like Doc” end card. The title, the #StopSmoking tag and the genre “Social Awareness” in the description show that it is a medical-college awareness film. It warns about the harm of smoking and has no brand or product promotion, so it is preventive.

“It hurts (award winning short film on smoking)”, 295 seconds, uploaded by “ashwin arya”. The description says it won 1st place in a Mumbai University competition. The film opens on a title card, “It Hurts”, over drifting cigarette-smoke-like swirls. The scenes show college students sitting on a stone wall with phones and books, a young man sitting alone with a bag, a woman in a blue dress in a home living room and a corridor, and an end shot of a gift box labelled “My Love For you” with a dark burnt-looking mark on the heart. No brand, no product promotion, and no glamorization of smoking was seen. The title, the smoke-themed opening, the “short film on smoking” tag and the end shot suggest a story about how smoking hurts the people around the smoker, so it is preventive.

“Kingfisher Oo La La La Le O TVC #1 - 2015 (90 sec)”, 93 seconds, uploaded by the channel “Kingfisher Packaged Drinking Water”. It is a surrogate ad: the Kingfisher beer brand is advertised through a “packaged drinking water” channel and a cricket “Good Times partner” campaign, with no alcohol shown. The description says “The Good Times last longer!” and “Kingfisher is the Good Times partner of Royal Challengers Bangalore, Mumbai Indians, Rajasthan Royals, Delhi Daredevils, Sunrisers Hyderabad and Kings XI Punjab”, and it uses the hashtag #UnitedByGoodTimes. The film shows cricketers in IPL team jerseys singing the jingle “Oo La La La Le O” in a car, a living room, a barbecue, a dressing room and a team bus. Caption lines: “are you ready for the good times” and “ul ulo ul yeah”. The end montage has a Kingfisher Premium logo with “GOOD TIMES PARTNER #UnitedbyKingfisher”. It ties the Kingfisher brand to fun, friendship, cricket and celebrity, which makes the brand attractive. No warning or anti-alcohol message was seen. The surrogate setting (a Kingfisher Premium logo on a “Good Times” cricket campaign) is also why this belongs with the alcohol brand ads.

“Tuborg Zero Advert Open for Fun”, 41 seconds, uploaded by “4adsindia” as an Indian ad. It is a surrogate ad: Tuborg is a beer brand, and the product shown is the non-alcoholic “Tuborg Zero” under the same brand name. Scenes: a bright wedding or party hall with guests, a hand passing a Tuborg bottle, two women reacting with surprise, a night dance floor under a tent, and a crowd with Tuborg banners. The end card shows the Tuborg Zero bottle with the logo “TUBORG ZERO - OPEN FOR FUN”, the line “Non Alcoholic Malt Beverage” and a Facebook.com/TuborgIndia link. Captions: “I got”, “Tube Zero.”, “Tube Zero. Hoping for fun.” (noisy). The ad links the brand with parties, dancing, celebration and fun, so it makes the brand attractive. No health warning or discouraging message was seen.

“Vodka Smirnoff commercial Old Indian Doordarshan Ad”, 91 seconds, uploaded by “All About 90’s Life”, an archived 1990s Indian TV ad. The channel’s overlay text reads “Missing 90’s era & old days? Relive the moments @ /notout90s” (the uploader’s own overlay, not part of the ad). Brand: Smirnoff vodka. The ad is a stylised, dreamlike scene: a man in a brown jacket sitting at a bar, a surreal masked and costumed dance sequence with people in period dress, a person dipping their head into a bowl at a candlelit table, close-ups of men drinking and a dance with swirling skirts. The end shows a Smirnoff vodka bottle next to a glass of cola with a lemon slice. The ad presents vodka as stylish, mysterious and sophisticated, and shows it being poured, drunk and mixed, which makes the brand attractive and encourages trial. No warning or anti-alcohol message was seen in the sampled frames. The uploader describes it as a “scary ad”, and it is an old third-party upload of the original commercial, so it could be excluded under strict rules for non-original uploads.

Hindi short film “NASHA NAHI NAASH HAI (SHORT FILM ON LIQUOR CONSUMPTION)”, 390 seconds, uploaded by “Sakshi communication”. The description says it was “initiated by the Government of Bihar to reduce liquor consumption”. The title card reads “NASHA NAHI NASH HAI / नशा नही नाश है”. The story is about a boy who is good at studies but is suspended from school because his drunk father could not pay the fees, and the father sells his books for liquor. Visuals: a village family scene with women and a child, a man arguing with his wife and son at home, a man holding up a mangalsutra, a woman in a sari, a young man speaking to an older man, a group of villagers, and a bearded man in glasses speaking to camera. The English subtitles read “mangalsutra, I’ll take care of it.”, “You want the mangalsutra, right? Let’s attack”, “I have surely felt that it destroys not just one” and “be free from addiction.” It shows liquor addiction wrecking a family’s money and a child’s education, and it ends with a call to be free from addiction, with no brand and no product promotion.

“A commercial for ‘Vimal Pan Masala’”, 43 seconds, uploaded by “After Studio” (description: produced by Cutting Edge Films, post by ‘after’ studio). Brand: Vimal Pan Masala. This is likely a surrogate ad, because pan masala brands are often used to advertise the brand name of tobacco (gutka) products, but the ad itself shows only pan masala. The film is a glossy, festive spot: a man in a cream kurta in a bright room (the opening), a smiling close-up, a silhouetted dance in warm light, people walking through a misty field at dusk, and a Holi-style colour celebration with riders on decorated elephants in front of a palace wall. Hindi subtitles from the song: "चढ़ी धुन जिया में हमरे केसरिया" and "रिश्तों का और अभी तो यह सिर्फ शुरुआत है". End card: the Vimal Pan Masala pack with the slogan “Daane Daane mein kesar ka dum” ("दाने दाने में केसर का दम"), with a small disclaimer strip at the bottom reading “NOT FOR MINORS. 0% TOBACCO NO ADDED NICOTINE” (the Hindi warning text next to it is partly unclear). The ad links the brand to celebration, colour, relationships and joy, which makes it attractive. The small disclaimer does not change the main message.

“Budweiser - Let your sound be seen. #BeAKing”, 30 seconds, uploaded by “Campaigns of the world”. The description says it is “Budweiser’s first Made-in-India TVC” about how music gives real freedom to millennials, with the hashtag #BeAKing. The ad opens with a young woman getting ready in front of a mirror in a small bathroom, then moves into a dim, warm-lit club or party with a dancing crowd and a person with a microphone cable. A red Budweiser bow-tie shape draws across the frames. On-screen text: “STAY TRUE TO YOUR BEAT”, “Be a King”, then the Budweiser logo with “× EXPERIENCES ×” on the end card. No bottle or drinking is shown in the sampled frames, so it is an indirect brand-image ad. It ties the Budweiser beer brand to music, nightlife, freedom, confidence and being a “King”, which makes the brand attractive. No warning or anti-alcohol message was seen.

“Bira 91: #MakePlay (full ad)”, 105 seconds, uploaded by the brand’s own channel, Bira 91. The description introduces Bira 91 as a “refreshingly modern beer brand, Imagined in India” that aims to bring more colour and flavour to beer. The film shows a woman commuting in a grey, dull subway train among people who stare at their phones and wear earphones. A stylised, colourful transformation follows: the carriage fills with bright ribbons of colour, cartoon-masked dancers and a woman laughing and playing in the middle. It then cuts to the same woman sitting at a bar with a glass of beer in front of her, the one place in the sampled frames where the product appears. The ad contrasts a dull routine with colour, play and fun, and links the beer brand to that, which makes it attractive. No warning or anti-alcohol message was seen. I did not catch a legible end card or logo in the sampled frames.

“Siggnature Finest Pan Masala | A Premium Product From Dilbagh”, 15 seconds, uploaded by “DB Siggnature”, the brand’s own channel. The description calls it “the finest pan masala”, “a premium product from Dilbagh”, made “with handpicked spices” and adds “Come taste the legacy and taste of success.” Brand: DB Siggnature (Dilbagh). This is likely a surrogate or brand-extension ad, because the “Dilbagh” name belongs to a tobacco (gutka) maker, but the video itself shows only pan masala. The film is a cinematic horse-racing spot: jockeys in blue, checked and yellow silks racing across a field, a close-up of a jockey in goggles, a man’s determined face looking into the distance, then a pack shot of a blue tin “Siggnature - Finest Pan Masala - A Premium Product from Dilbagh” with a jockey riding off in the background. Caption lines: “Some win for themselves” and “themselves Signature Finest Pan”, and an end line, “Mijaaj Ji’s Premium Product from Dilbagh”. Small on-screen disclaimers read “Stunts performed by professionals under controlled environment. Do not imitate. No Animals were harmed in making of this Film.” and, at the bottom with a green dot, “Chewing of Pan Masala is injurious to health. Not for Minors. 0% Tobacco & No Added Nicotine”. The ad ties the brand to winning, success and prestige, which makes it attractive. The small required warning does not change the main message.

“CONTESSA RUM”, 92 seconds, uploaded by “Corcoise Films”; the description gives only “Director: Prasoon Pandey”. Brand: Contessa Rum (Radico). This is a direct alcohol ad, not a surrogate ad: the rum bottle and drinking are shown. The film is a comic pirate story. A pirate ship in a stormy sea, then a rowdy tavern table of pirates laughing with candles, pistols and a rope of pearls, a pirate with a woman on his lap and a Contessa bottle on the table, a pirate drinking from a glass, a bearded pirate raising a glass with a bottle beside him, and a wide table shot with the bottle at the centre. The end card shows the Contessa Rum bottle with the tagline “What men want” and the Radico logo. The auto-captions are Spanish and misheard (“es señorita”, “a esta lista que estaba”), so I have not quoted them. The ad links drinking rum with camaraderie, masculinity, adventure and fun, and the tagline presents it as a desire, which makes it attractive. No warning or anti-alcohol message was seen in the sampled frames.

“1998: London Pilsner”, 31 seconds, uploaded by “Guruprasad Gp”, an archived 1990s Indian beer commercial (the description only repeats the title). Brand: London Pilsner beer. It is a direct alcohol ad, not a surrogate. The film opens on the embossed “LONDON PILSNER” label, then shows a lively pub or restaurant with people at checked tablecloths and a waiter or guest carrying a beer mug, close shots of people laughing and holding glasses, a bottle being opened with a cap popping off, and a frothy pour. The end card shows a London Pilsner bottle next to a full foamy mug with the slogan “LP. Live it up!!!” in script. The ad links drinking the beer to a fun, social, high-spirited night out and ends on an invitation to “live it up”, which makes the brand attractive and encourages trial. No warning or anti-alcohol message was seen in the sampled frames.

"तंबाखूला नाही म्हणा | National Tobacco Control Programme | राष्ट्रीय तंबाखू नियंत्रण कार्यक्रम [NTCP]", 37 seconds, uploaded by “PHD Maha Health IEC” (Government of Maharashtra, Public Health Department, State Health IEC Bureau, Pune), a Marathi anti-tobacco awareness video. Product: tobacco | Brand: not_applicable. The title card shows "राष्ट्रीय तंबाखू नियंत्रण कार्यक्रम (NTCP) NATIONAL TOBACCO CONTROL PROGRAMME" next to an illustration of a big cigarette with a red “no” sign in front of a house, and a red banner reading "तंबाखू- तोंडाचा कॅन्सर.." (“tobacco - mouth cancer”). The captions, which are partly garbled Hindi auto-captions of Marathi speech, mention oral cancer and tobacco use: "मी एक तोंडाचा कॅन्सर" (“I am a mouth cancer”), "तोंडा कॅन्सर से दोगुना है", "एक शाहिद तंबाकू चगंदी पैन गुटखा पैन" and "मृत्यू हो तो आदत सोडा आरोग्य विभाग महाराष्ट्र" (“if it is death, quit the habit”). The end cards show the "सार्वजनिक आरोग्य विभाग, महाराष्ट्र शासन" logo, "राज्य आरोग्य शिक्षण व संपर्क विभाग, पुणे" and social media handles. It is preventive: a government health video that links tobacco to mouth cancer and death and urges people to quit, with no brand or product promotion.

“Public Service Announcement on Tobacco Control featuring Shri Rahul Dravid”, 40 seconds, uploaded by PHFICHANNEL (Public Health Foundation of India). The description says it is a bilingual set of PSAs launched by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, the WHO Country Office for India, PHFI and HRIDAY, featuring Rahul Dravid as India’s Ambassador for Tobacco Control (the name comes from the title and description, not from his face). Product: tobacco | Brand: not_applicable. The film opens on a newspaper-style montage of a cricketer batting, with the Hindi headline "राहुल द्रविड़ : भारत की भरोसेमंद दीवार" and the strapline "राहुल द्रविड़ तंबाकू नियंत्रण अभियान के ब्रांड एंबेसडर नियुक्त". A man in a dark polo then speaks to camera, followed by the main frame: the same man at a cricket ground with the Hindi text "ज़िन्दगी में लम्बी पारी खेलना चाहते हैं? तंबाकू सेवन से दूर रहें: तंबाकू जानलेवा है!" (“Want to play a long innings in life? Stay away from tobacco: tobacco is deadly!”) and the logo “NO MORE TOBACCO 21C”, with the ministry, WHO and HRIDAY logos at the bottom. The end card reads "स्वास्थ्य एवं परिवार कल्याण मंत्रालय भारत सरकार द्वारा जनहित में जारी" (“issued in public interest by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India”). “Tulsi Mix Pan Masala | तुलसी पान मसाला | old ad tulsi mix old advertisement” is a 66-second old Indian TV ad from the Doordarshan era, uploaded by the archive channel “Unforgettable 90’s”. The upload description reads “Old Doordarshan Tv Ad । Tulsi Pan Masala । तुलसी पान मसाला”. The film is a music-video style ad for Tulsi Mix pan masala. “Goa – Iconic Pan Masala Ad Film | Paresh Rawal & Mohan Joshi | Directed by A H Siddiqui” is a 62-second Indian TV ad from 1997 for Goa pan masala. It is uploaded by the archive channel “Rafat Films Entertainment”, and its description names the actors Paresh Rawal and Mohan Joshi. It is a short comedy skit shot at a Mumbai dock. Workers carry cartons toward a ship while armed guards watch, and a customs-style officer in khaki confronts a man in a grey suit and dark glasses: "हैंड क्या हो रहा है तुम स्मगलिंग कर...", "एक्सपोर्ट कर रहे हो अमेरिका केनिया बांग्लादेश मुंबई...". A shot of Goa sachets on a carton shows the contents of the shipment. The man says "मिलता और आप बाहर भेज रहे हैं सर हम वहां भी खिलाते हैं यहां" and, after tasting it, "खाइए आज तो बड़ा मजा आया गोवा खाके". The end card shows “J. M. GROUP OF COMPANIES Present” above the “Goa 1000” pan masala pack, with the closing line "छोड़ दिया गोवा पान मसाला ऊंची खुशबू ऊंचा स्वाद" (“Goa pan masala, high fragrance, high taste”). A faint line of small print starting “Statutory ...” sits at the bottom of the end card, and it looks like a health warning. The ad is about smuggling a product that is actually Goa pan masala, and it makes the product look desirable and in demand, with the brand and the slogan on the end card, so it is promotional. The ad shows only pan masala.

“Goa Pan Masala Ad (Second Version) | Featuring Paresh Rawal | Directed by A H Siddiqui” is a 61-second old Indian TV commercial for Goa 1000 pan masala. It is uploaded by the archive channel “Rafat Films Entertainment”, and its description names the actor Paresh Rawal. The ad is a comic skit set at a crowded wedding hall. Burned-in Hindi subtitles show a man in a grey suit telling the host "था मैं दहेज का विरोधी हूं लेकिन मेरे बारातियों की खातिरदारी 24 कैरेट से करना अगर तुमने देरी की तो हम उठ जाएंगे", and later, after a tip-off about a "हवामाला" (“ruckus”) at the venue: "हम गोवा और खुशी दोनों साथ-साथ बांटते हैं". A man in a pink turban and a suit then tastes the product and says "कुछ नहीं बदला। वाह वही खुशबू" (“nothing has changed, wow, the same fragrance”), and the wedding crowd cheers. A later line says "बैठ जा। पहले गोवा 1000 खिलाओ फिर बैठूंगा फिर ऊपर। आज तो बड़ा मजा आया". The end card shows the Goa 1000 sachet and a man tipping his head back with a sachet. Its text reads "गोवा 1000 पान मसाला ऊंची खुशबू ऊंचा स्वाद" (“high fragrance, high taste”), and a small line at the bottom starts “STATUTORY ... IS TO HEALTH”, which looks like a statutory health warning. The ad presents the pan masala as the thing that settles a conflict and brings joy to a celebration, which is promotional. The tiny required warning does not change that. The ad shows only pan masala.

“GOA Gutkha Ad.” is a 34-second Indian TV commercial for Goa gutkha (a tobacco-containing chewing product) in the “Goa 000” style, uploaded by “MrGOAGUTKHA”. The description reads “gutkha bole GOA.....quality khaoo mast ho jaoo----ab 2 aur 3 rs mein !!!!!!!!” (“eat quality, get high, now at 2 and 3 rupees”). It is a comic scene at a pan shop. A man in a bright patterned shirt, gold chains and sunglasses bargains over price with the shopkeeper in a woollen cap. Burned-in Hindi captions carry the dialogue: "आ हा गुवा का भाव रप हो गया भैया अठनी ज्यादा", "ज्यादा क्यों गधे का भाव बड़ा है ना", "इसमें क्वालिटी कत्था डाले या ग्राहक को चूना लगाए क्वालिटी सुपारी खाओगे या कचरा, कश्मीरी केसर खाओगे या झमरी तलैया का घास", "तो अगर गवा का मजा चाहिए या ठत्री ज्यादा या चवानी छाप", "या चवानी छाप मसाला गोवा 000 अब में क्योंकि..." and "क्योंकि मर्दानगी की लामी अठनी में नहीं होती है" (“because manliness does not come for eight annas”). The frames show a small statutory warning line and the words “NOT FOR MINORS” at the bottom. The ad presents the product as the quality choice for a man, with a low price (2 and 3 rupees) and a link to manliness. That encourages purchase and makes use look desirable, which is promotional. The small warning does not change that.

“GOA Pan Masala | Iconic 1990 Ad in Sholay’s Gabbar Scene – ‘Kitne Aadmi The?’” is a 61-second old Indian TV ad for Goa 1000 pan masala, uploaded by the archive channel “Rafat Films Entertainment”. It is a parody of the famous bandit-gang scene from the film Sholay, shot in a rocky hill setting with men dressed as outlaws. The burned-in Hindi captions open with the parody line "कितने आदमी थे दो सरदार" and the replies “...नहीं आया पास लाओ पायला की सरदार”, followed by a lookalike outlaw chief pointing a gun at a man. A man then holds up a strip of Goa sachets: "पर सरदार आज से आप गुआ खाएंगे". The chief tastes it and is won over: "आपका गोवा खाया सरदार अच्छा आज तो बहुत मजा" (“I ate your Goa, chief, now that was a lot of fun”). The end card shows the Goa 1000 sachets and the brand logo, and the captions read "खाके सबको छोड़ दिया गोवा 1000 पान मसाला ऊंची खुशबू ऊंचा स्वाद" (“after eating it he let everyone go, Goa 1000 pan masala, high fragrance, high taste”). The ad uses a famous film scene to show a fearsome outlaw becoming friendly after chewing the product, so it makes the product look desirable and funny. That is promotional. It shows only pan masala.

“Goa Paan Masala TVC” is a 49-second Indian TV commercial for Goa 1000 pan masala, uploaded by “Coconutfilms1”. The description credits the client as Goa Paan Masala, the production house as Coconut Films and the producer as Tushar Raut, so it is the production company’s own upload of the commercial. The burned-in Hindi captions carry the dialogue: "मर्द म गोवा अभी ढाई रुपए को हो गया है भैया गोवा लिए हैं हवाई जहाज नहीं", "ज्यादा क्यों कथे का भाव बड़ा है ना तो इसमें क्वालिटी...", "क्वालिटी कथा डाले या ग्राहक को चूना लगाए क्वालिटी सुपारी खाओगे कश्मीरी केसर खाओगे या झुमरी तलैया का घास", and "तो अगर गवा का मजा चाहिए या ठत्री ज्यादा या चवानी छाप मसाला गोवा 1000". A pack shot of the Goa 1000 sachet follows, with the on-screen price offer "अब 2.50 रुपये में" and the line "अब ढाई रुपए क्योंकि मर्दानगी की नीलामी अठन्नी नीलामी अठन्नी में नहीं होती". The words “Statutory Warn...” run in small print at the bottom of the frames. The ad sells the product through a low price, a quality claim and the idea that manliness is not “auctioned for eight annas”, which is promotional. The small warning line does not change that. “Seagram’s Imperial Blue Superhits Music CDs” is a 30-second Indian TV commercial uploaded by “TV Ads Reviews”, a third-party channel. It is a surrogate ad for Imperial Blue whisky: it advertises “Superhits Music CDs” under the whisky’s brand name, with the “Seagram’s Imperial Blue Music CDs” logo in the corner of every frame. “India - Sponge (Hindi)” is a 36-second Indian anti-smoking public-service ad uploaded by Vital Strategies, a public-health organisation. The opening title card reads “Sponge / Hindi - 30 Sec”. The film shows a dark X-ray wall with a chest X-ray in which both lungs are yellow, like sponges, while a silhouetted man smokes. The burned-in Hindi subtitles carry the narration: "मनुष्य के स्पंज समान फेफड़े हवा सोखने के लिए बने हैं, बीड़ी सिगरेट का धुआं सोखने के लिए इस्तेमाल करते हैं, एक आम धूम्रपान करने वाले...". A hand then wrings a lung like a sponge and a thick brown tar drips into a glass beaker. The subtitle continues: "फेफड़ों को अगर आप निचोड़ कर देखें तो इतनी मात्रा में आपको... इतनी मात्रा में आपको साल भर का कैंसर पैदा करने वाला टार मिलेगा, इतना टार केवल..." (“a regular smoker’s lungs hold this much cancer-causing tar for a whole year”). The ad uses the sponge and tar images to show the physical damage of cigarette and bidi smoke, so it discourages smoking, which is preventive. It shows no tobacco brand.

“Ministry of Health and Family Welfare: Anti-Tobacco spot” is a 38-second government anti-smoking spot titled “Child”, uploaded by PIB India (the Press Information Bureau). The description says the ministry released it under the COTPA rules, and that it must be screened in movies whenever a smoking scene is shown. The opening title card reads “Child / SmokeFree / Hindi / 30 sec”. A little girl in a pink top draws a family picture with crayons, with the words “Lovey...” written on it. A father smokes at a table in an office, and a colleague says “Who doesn’t want happiness?”. Then at home he sits on a sofa with his daughter, cigarette in hand, and the English subtitles say “...cost? Smoking is expensive. Smoking is harmful to you. And for [others] too. Smoking will cost you dearly”. The girl looks up at him, and in a later shot he hugs her. A Hindi line on screen says "एक का धूम्रपान दूसरों के लिए भी घातक है" (“one person’s smoking is deadly for others too”). The ad uses the child and the family to show that smoking harms the smoker and the people around him, and that it is costly. It discourages smoking, which is preventive. It shows no tobacco brand.

“Dhuan: Anti-smoking spot of Ministry of Health and Family Welfare” is a 37-second government anti-smoking spot uploaded by PIB India (the Press Information Bureau). The English auto-subtitles are garbled but pick up lines such as “What has happ to this city Ashes”, “Why are you so Silent” and “Smoke ... let ...”. The ad shows the harm of second-hand smoke and says that smoking has a cost, which discourages smoking, so it is preventive. It shows no tobacco brand.

A clipping headline reads “A WORLDWIDE KILLER ON THE LOOSE”, and another reads “UNBEATEN AND IMMORTAL AT 200” over a batsman at the crease. The captions continue “deadly please stay away from tobacco” and “lead a healthy life, i do so should you, let us...”. The speaker, named in the title as Dravid, addresses the camera in a dark sports jacket. The closing card shows the slogan “WANT TO PLAY A LONG INNINGS IN LIFE? STAY AWAY FROM TOBACCO. TOBACCO KILLS!” with the “No More Tobacco 21C” logo, the credit “Young people must take the lead in eliminating Tobacco in 21st Century / Mr Rahul Dravid, Tobacco Control Brand Ambassador for Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India”, and a final white card, “ISSUED IN PUBLIC INTEREST BY / Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Government of India / National Tobacco Control Programme / Choose LIFE, Not Tobacco.” The ad uses a cricketing icon to tell young people to stay away from tobacco, so it is preventive. “India - Tobacco Control – Main Bhi Sunita (Sunita 2.0) - English” is a 30-second government anti-tobacco testimonial ad uploaded by Vital Strategies. The description says it is a testimonial campaign about a family hit by cancer from chewing khaini, a smokeless tobacco. It is told from the wife’s point of view and was launched in 17 Indian languages by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, to air in TV programmes and films from 10 August 2024 under the tobacco-free film rules. The film shows a man in a hospital gown, captioned “Om Prakash, Age 38”. His wife, captioned “Sunita (Wife), Age 30”, sits in a hospital waiting area. Next comes a close-up of the man’s face with a large cancerous swelling on his jaw. A later shot is captioned “2 weeks after surgery”, showing him on a bed with oxygen tubes while his wife stands beside him. She covers her face, crying. The Hindi-transliterated English subtitles carry her story: "माय हस्बैंड वास एडिक्टेड टू चूइंग नी सिंस द एज ऑफ 18..." (“my husband was addicted to chewing khaini since the age of 18...”), "हैज अ डेंजरस कैंसर", "नाइट्स थिंकिंग ऑफ आवर अनसर्टेन फ्यूचर", and "हैज रूइंड आवर लाइव्स स्मोकलेस टोबैको नी गुटका जर्दा पान मसाला डिस्ट्रॉयज" (“smokeless tobacco, khaini, gutka, zarda, pan masala destroys...”). The end card reads “QUIT TOBACCO TODAY / FOR HELP CALL 1-800-11-2356 (TOLL FREE)” with the logos of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and the National Tobacco Control Programme. “Oral Cancer Awareness” is a 78-second Indian anti-smoking film uploaded by the Indian Cancer Society, whose logo sits in the corner of the closing frames. The description reads “Indian Cancer Society film on peril of smoking”. The film is a series of hospital scenes and patient portraits. A man in a wheelchair waits in a crowded hospital registration hall, a bearded older man looks at the camera with a feeding tube in his nose, an older woman with missing teeth looks straight into the lens, an IV drip and syringe are shown in close-up, and a woman lies in a hospital bed with an oxygen mask. The mood then shifts to dark swirling smoke, with a Hindi word on screen. The word is cut off but looks like "समझाइए" (“explain”). The end card reads "हर सिगरेट कैंसर रोग की ओर एक कदम है" (“every cigarette is a step towards cancer”) beside the Indian Cancer Society logo. The film shows the suffering of cancer patients and ties each cigarette to cancer, which discourages smoking, so it is preventive. It shows no tobacco brand.

“Drink & Drive Accident Short Film | Traffic Rules Awareness India #trafficpolice” is a 42-second Hindi road-safety short film uploaded by “Churru Chaplin”. The description says the film shows the dangers of drink-driving, asks people not to drink and drive, and ends with “Don’t Drink And Drive – Safe Drive, Save Life”. The title card reads "आखिरी सफर" (“the last journey”). A young man drives at night with a beer bottle in hand while two friends ride with him. The burned-in Hindi subtitles carry the dialogue: "मजा आ गया। अबे मजा अभी नहीं आया। मजा तो तुझे अब आएगा कि अपनी ड्राइविंग...", then "अबे भाई सामने पुलिस। अबे तू टेंशन मत ले। मैं हूं ना।" and "देख बचा दिया ना तेरे भाई ने।" (“see, your brother saved you”). A bottom-right line, "शराब पीना सेहत के लिए हानिकारक है" (“drinking alcohol is harmful to health”), stays on screen throughout. After the police scene a blurred shot cuts to the text "वाहन चलाते समय ..." (“while driving...”), then a “Drive Safe” key ring with the slogan "सड़क सुरक्षा - जीवन रक्षा" (“road safety - protecting life”), and a final white card with a police logo and the line "हमारा लक्ष्य सुगम, सुरक्षित, सुरक्षद यातायात" (“our goal: smooth, safe traffic”). The film shows the risk of drink-driving, ends on road-safety messages and the police logo, and discourages the behaviour, so it is preventive. It shows an alcohol bottle but no brand, and it is a public-safety film, not an alcohol ad.

“Don’t drink and drive - Hindi” is a 35-second government road-safety ad uploaded by MorthIndia, the channel of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. The description says drunk driving takes thousands of lives every year and affects family and friends too, and that the ad was issued in public interest by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Government of India. The opening card reads “Title: Drinking Drive / Duration: 30 Sec. / Language: Hindi”. The film shows two plastic cups of a fizzy amber drink next to a bowl of nuts in a car’s cup holder, and a tyre spinning on a dark road. A man in a light-green shirt drives with a laughing friend in a patterned shirt who holds a cup of the drink, and a third friend in the back holds another cup. The camera cuts to the spinning wheel again, with Hindi text: "अल्कोहल का असर: सोचने की क्षमता घटाता है, प्रतिक्रिया करने का समय बढ़ा देता है" (“the effect of alcohol: it reduces the ability to think and increases reaction time”). A black card follows: "शराब पीकर गाड़ी चलाना यानी मौत को दावत" (“driving after drinking means inviting death”). The end card reads "सड़क परिवहन और राजमार्ग मंत्रालय, भारत सरकार द्वारा जनहित में जारी" (“issued in public interest by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Government of India”), with the national emblem. The ad shows the effect of alcohol on a driver and says drink-driving is inviting death, which is preventive. It shows no alcohol brand.
